purpose: VibeVoice-ASR diverse-subset WER gate: hipEngine vs torch-GPU bf16 reference on matched inputs
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)

protocol.dataset: LibriSpeech test-clean (OpenSLR), 50 clips spread one-per-chapter across 23 speakers
protocol.audio: 16 kHz FLAC resampled to 24 kHz float PCM (scipy resample_poly)
protocol.lanes: matched frozen-request bench protocol (hash-checked request.npz, subprocess isolation), greedy, max_new_tokens 256
protocol.scoring: jiwer process_words WER after Whisper EnglishTextNormalizer; structured-output Content extracted

findings: hipEngine 1.978% vs torch bf16 4.586% aggregate WER on the same frozen requests; hipEngine matches or beats torch on every clip where per-clip WER differs (9/50)
on 260-123440 the torch eager-attention lane produced a completely wrong transcript (WER 1.0) while hipEngine scored 0.0

both lanes are far below the model card's published 2.20% test-clean row; NOT a leaderboard-comparable number - a 50-clip easy-skewed subset, and possibly a different audio/chunking protocol; the load-bearing comparison is hip-vs-torch under the identical matched-request protocol
transcript differences are punctuation/possessive-level bf16-vs-fp16 rounding divergence, as in the single-speaker parity run
corrections: CORRECTION 2026-09-14: the *_wer_pct fields originally held jiwer fractions (0-1), not percentages; they are now the true percentages and the fractions are kept alongside as *_wer_fraction. The Q4-vs-bf16 equality and the hip-vs-torch ordering are unchanged; only the scale was wrong (100x).
